narration: Thank God, His people keep growing! Every Sunday, more families fill our churches, and more little feet come running through the doors.

But here's the question every priest quietly asks. Who came today? Who didn't? And who has been missing for weeks, without anyone noticing? Paper lists get lost. Names get forgotten. And the people who need a phone call the most are the easiest to miss.
on-screen text: Who came today? Who is missing?

narration: That's why we built Amoinee. It comes from the Coptic word for "Come!" It helps every church know its people, care for them, and never lose one of them. So let's see how it works, step by step.

It all starts with the members. Create your profile just once. Your name, your phone, your email, your address, and your church, which you simply start typing and pick from the list. It takes a minute, and it works on any phone.

You also choose whether to turn on face check-in. Say yes, sign the consent, and take a quick face setup. Say no, and that's perfectly fine, because there are other ways to check in. And you can always take it back: turn it off, and your face data is deleted.

At the church door stands the Amoinee kiosk, a tablet on a stand that an admin signs in. Before the service, it just shows what's coming next, with the camera switched off. When check-in opens, it wakes up all by itself.

Now watch. Someone walks in, looks at the screen, and in a second it says, welcome, by name. It records that you're here. It even checks that it's a real face and not a photo. And it takes one person at a time, so everyone gets their moment.
Prefer not to use your face? Just scan the QR code on the kiosk with your phone, and you're checked in. The code changes every minute, so it can't be passed around.
Or type the three-digit code of the day in the app. Three simple ways to check in, and nobody is ever left at the door.
And members can open My History at any time, to see every service they attended, with the date and time.
Now let's see what Abouna and the servants get. This is where attendance turns into care.

The Today screen is live. As people arrive, their names pop up with the arrival time, whether they came by face, QR code or the daily code. You see who is on time and who is late, who is still missing, and you can check someone in by hand with one tap.

Services open by themselves. Set your weekly events once, like the Divine Liturgy on Sunday morning, and check-in opens and closes on time. Each church has its own list of services, like Vespers, Bible Study, Sunday School, choir, youth, and family meetings. Add or remove your own, any time.

The Members page keeps every person in one place, numbered and easy to search by name, phone, city or church. Filter by men, women, deacons, or visitors. Open any profile to add a photo, make someone a deacon, call or text with one tap, see their family, and write private notes that only your church's admins can read.

And now, the heart of Amoinee: the Attendance Sheet. At the top, a short summary in plain words. How many people came, the average per service, and how many need a follow-up. Four big numbers show the average attendance, the attendance rate, how many attend every week, and how many need a call.

Below, simple charts. Who came at least once. Attendance over time, compared with the period before. How many attend every week, how many come often, sometimes, or rarely. What time people arrive. And men, women and deacons at each service. Pick any period you like, or a single kind of service.

Then the register. One little square for every person at every service, like the paper register of old, but alive. And the ranked list puts everyone in order, from the people who attend every single week, with a medal for the top three, to those who could use a gentle call. You'll see streaks, the last visit, and how late they usually arrive. On a phone, a compact view shows one line per person.

When someone misses a few Sundays, Amoinee gently marks them "Follow up needed", so nobody slips through the cracks. Then your servants can add labels: Called, Visited, Needs prayer, Traveling, Sick, Away at college. They can snooze a reminder when it's not the right time, and everyone sees who is taking care of whom. You can even create your own labels.
And when that person comes back, they show up under Welcome Back, so you can greet them warmly. You'll also see who is new, and whose birthday is this week, so every member feels remembered.
Because behind every name is a person who may be waiting for a call. A word of encouragement, a visit, a prayer, can bring someone home.

Need a report? With one tap, Abouna gets a one-page summary to print or save as a PDF, in English or in Arabic. And the full data goes to Excel, with the register, the follow-up list, and the label history.

Access is simple and safe. Anyone can ask to become an admin of their church, and an existing admin approves it. Each admin sees only their own church. The super admin can switch between churches. Notes and labels are never public, never on the kiosk, and every face is stored only with consent.
on-screen text: Each church sees its own people

narration: Because every soul matters, and no one should be forgotten. Amoinee. Come, let us worship.
on-screen text: Every one of God's people, known and cared for.
